title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the 2020 Committee report by pledging to strengthen public standards for artificial intelligence, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and ethical use. It plans to work with industry, academia, and civil society to develop regulations, support research, and ensure AI systems meet safety and fairness criteria.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is developing guidelines to oversee how artificial intelligence can be used in the qualifications sector, aiming to ensure that AI tools support fair and transparent assessment practices. The policy intends to maintain exam integrity, protect against bias, and keep the use of AI aligned with national education standards.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop artificial intelligence systems, exploring the benefits and challenges of such practices. It evaluates the impact on creators, users, and the AI industry, offering guidance to balance innovation with copyright protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government outlines its plan to address the concerns raised by the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence in the report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It commits to strengthening regulation, boosting investment in AI research, improving transparency and oversight, and ensuring that the UK remains a global leader in safe and responsible AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference for a committee charged with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards and includes a FAQ section to guide the process. It outlines the committee’s objectives, scope, and procedures for assessing AI’s impact on society and policy.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines CSPL’s views on how AI should be regulated, including recommendations for policy and oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how artificial intelligence will change the rules that govern medical products, focusing on safety and effectiveness. It also describes how the principles from the AI White Paper will be used to guide regulators and companies in developing and approving new medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defence organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑enabled entity for its size. It plans to develop and deploy AI technologies that enhance operational capabilities while ensuring ethical, secure, and responsible use.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to use AI to improve safety, efficiency, and sustainability. It also outlines steps to manage risks such as privacy concerns, safety issues, and potential job disruptions.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright works have been used to train and develop AI systems, and evaluates the compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act’s Section 137. It highlights current practices, challenges, and recommendations for balancing innovation with intellectual property rights.
